title: Grateful Dead Live at Dillon Gym - Princeton University on 1971-04-17
lineage: R3 > Technics RS-1506 > TEAC AN-300 DOLBY DECODE > GRACE DESIGN LUNATEC V3 PRE ONLY > KORG MR-1000 > DSD DDF 1BIT 5.644mhZ > AUDIO GATE SW DISEMINATION > 24BIT wav
source: MSR> R1? > R2 MAXELL UD35-90 3.75 IPS (Dick Latvala) Technics RS-1506 > R3 TANDBERG TD20A 7.5IPS

ai_review.summary: A super‑hot April ’71 college‑gym show captured on a pristine soundboard mix, highlighted by Pigpen’s blazing vocals and a monster Casey Jones.
ai_review.review: The performance is widely praised as tight, high‑energy and full of standout moments – especially Pigpen’s soulful delivery, the searing “Casey Jones” and the psychedelic jam on “Good Lovin’”. The Sirmick‑restored soundboard recording is described as crisp and exceptionally clear for a 1971 source, though one reviewer notes pitch‑correction quirks and occasional speed wobble. Overall the show delivers a thrilling snapshot of the Dead’s early ’71 magic.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers award five stars for both performance and audio, citing tight playing and excellent sound quality; a single three‑star review points out pitch issues, pulling the weighted average slightly lower.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Audio praised as crisp, dynamic and well‑balanced for a 1971 college‑gym capture; however one reviewer mentions pitch‑correction problems, speed wobble and occasional channel swaps in some versions.

show_quality.setlist_flow: First set opens solidly with Truckin' and builds through Pigpen‑centric numbers; second set mixes psychedelic jams (Good Lovin') with tight rockers, ending on a high‑energy finale.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia’s guitar work is praised as tight and expressive, with extra flair noted on “Beat It On Down the Line”.
band_member_comments.Keys: Ron "Pig" McKernan’s organ/keyboard parts are highlighted as high‑caliber, though a few songs are said to sound better without piano.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill Kreutzmann’s drumming is described as hot, in the pocket and driving the band with an intense yet relaxed feel.
